explanation: The retry counter increment was moved from before the `< max_retries` check to inside it, changing the semantics: previously `task_retries` was incremented on every failure (so the condition was `<= total_retries`), but now it is only incremented when a retry is actually scheduled (condition `< max_retries`), which could cause an off-by-one difference in retry count behavior and may interact incorrectly with the new `_retry_failed_task` helper that duplicates the same logic independently.
